title: Vinted Seller Cancelled My Order to Sell It for More — Can You Do Anything?
intro: If a Vinted seller cancels your paid order and then relists the same item at a higher price, there is no way to force them to honour the sale — Vinted lets either side cancel an order any time before the item is shipped, and when a seller cancels you are refunded automatically. What you can do is use the one lever Vinted actually gives you: edit the automatic negative feedback the cancellation leaves on their profile so it spells out what happened, report the account, and block it. Here is exactly how that works, why the trick keeps happening, and how to spot a serial canceller before you buy.
meta_description: Vinted seller cancelled your order then relisted it for more? You can't force the sale, but you can edit the auto-feedback, report the seller, and avoid repeat cancellers. Here's how.
author: Supervint Team
cta_text: Get alerted the moment genuine listings appear — before someone else's deal gets pulled

body.heading: What just happened — and why Vinted allows it
paragraphs: You found the item, paid, and the order was confirmed. Then either the seller went quiet and cancelled out of nowhere, or they messaged first with a story about the price being wrong. Either way, within minutes or hours the exact same listing — same photos, same description — reappears at a higher price. It is one of the most common complaints on r/vinted and r/vintedUK right now, in threads with titles like "Seller cancelled to sell for more", "Order cancelled to sell it for a higher price", "Seller cancelled order to relist for higher price", and "Seller lied just to repost it for five times as much". The reply that keeps coming up underneath them: it happens all the time.

It is allowed because of how Vinted's cancellation rules are written. Vinted's own help states that an order can only be cancelled by either the buyer or the seller if the item has not been shipped yet — so until the seller prints the label and posts the parcel, they can pull the order. After a cancellation, the seller can press "Re-upload item" in the conversation screen and the listing is live again, ready to catch a higher offer. In other words, a seller who decides they listed too cheaply, or who gets a better offer from someone else, can cancel your paid order and put it straight back up.

There is meant to be a consequence built in. Vinted's rules say that a member who cancels an order manually "might receive automatic negative feedback" — and its feedback page confirms that automatic negative feedback is added when the item is not shipped on time, or when the seller or buyer cancels the order manually. That is the part serial cancellers try to dodge, and the reason so many buyers say no negative feedback ever appeared: the seller can pick a cancellation reason, or claim the cancellation was agreed, so the automatic mark never shows on their profile.

body.heading: The one lever that actually helps: edit the automatic feedback
paragraphs: Here is the thing most buyers do not realise. When a seller cancels your order, Vinted leaves automatic negative feedback on their profile — on your behalf. And as the buyer, you can edit or delete that feedback. Open the seller's profile, tap their star rating, find your feedback, and press Edit.

Use it. Turn the generic auto-note into a short, factual record of what happened — for example: "Cancelled my paid order minutes after I bought it, then relisted the same item at a higher price." Keep it factual and polite. Vinted only removes feedback that breaks its own rules — bad language, threats, harassment, or private information — so a calm, accurate description stays up and is what every future buyer reads before they buy.

There is one trade-off worth knowing before you edit anything. If you leave the automatic negative feedback exactly as Vinted generated it, the seller usually cannot leave feedback back — several buyers confirm that if you do not touch it, the seller cannot retaliate on your profile. If you edit it into a detailed warning, you open the door for the seller to reply or to rate you. So decide which matters more: a quiet mark that protects your own profile, or a loud warning that protects the next buyer. The community's usual advice is to leave the auto-feedback untouched if you want to stay untouchable yourself.

One catch: if the seller cancelled by claiming the cancellation was "agreed with you", or if you agreed to it, the automatic negative feedback can be removed entirely — which is exactly how repeat cancellers keep a clean-looking record.

body.heading: How to report a seller who cancels to relist higher
paragraphs: Reporting is worth doing, as long as you go in with realistic expectations. Use the report option on the listing or the seller's profile. If you have screenshots — proof you paid for the original listing, and the new higher-priced listing of the same item with the same photos — describe that clearly. Some buyers report that Vinted acted on a clear case of exactly this behaviour, and there are documented cases of an account being taken down after a report. Just as many buyers report that nothing visible happens. Treat it as a shot worth taking rather than a guaranteed fix.

The important rule while you do it: keep everything on Vinted. Do not move to another messaging app to discuss it, and never send money outside the platform. If the seller asks you to pay anything off-app, that is the moment to stop and report.

body.heading: The bait-and-switch version: "pay me more or I'll cancel"
paragraphs: Sometimes the cancellation is not silent. The seller messages after you have already paid — asking for a few more pounds, or telling a hard-luck story and asking you to send money directly. Both are pushes for a payment outside the agreed sale. You already have a confirmed, paid order at the agreed price, so you do not owe anything more, and you should never pay outside Vinted: the moment a payment leaves the platform, Buyer Protection no longer applies and your money is effectively gone.

The correct move is simple. Politely decline and hold your ground. If they then cancel, you are refunded automatically and the sale is over. If they ship, the original deal stands. Do not offer to top up the price to keep the sale alive — that is exactly the outcome the message is fishing for.

body.heading: What you cannot do — so you do not waste your time
paragraphs: You cannot force the sale. There is no mechanism on Vinted to compel a seller to ship an item, and because either side can cancel before posting, the platform treats the cancellation as valid. Buyers who contacted support about a cancelled order commonly report being told that feedback is only possible on completed transactions — which is precisely why the auto-feedback edit above is the lever that matters.

You also cannot leave a normal new review on a cancelled order, because Vinted only lets you rate completed orders. Editing the automatic feedback already sitting on the seller's profile is the exception, and it is the route most buyers miss.

Finally, do not keep messaging the seller who cancelled to relist. If they have already chosen a higher price over your paid order, the odds they will quietly honour the old one are low — and chasing them risks getting blocked, which closes off your ability to report or review the profile. Report, edit if you choose to, then block and move on.

body.heading: How to spot a serial canceller before you buy
paragraphs: Check the seller's Reviews, not just their star average. Look for a run of automatic "seller cancelled the order" notes. A profile with several cancellations is someone who does this habitually, even if their overall rating still looks respectable.

Watch for the same listing being bought and reappearing. If an item you have been watching keeps showing as unavailable and then coming back at the same or a higher price, the seller is cycling buyers rather than selling.

Be extra cautious with rare, collectible or high-demand items priced clearly below the market. Those are the listings where a seller is most likely to get a better offer and cancel on you to take it. If being cancelled on would leave you out of pocket or deeply disappointed, factor that in before you commit.

And if you are on the other side of this and simply change your mind, let the seller cancel the order rather than cancelling it yourself — Vinted's automatic negative feedback attaches to whoever presses the button, so cancelling yourself risks a mark on your own profile.

faq.question: Is it against Vinted's rules for a seller to cancel and relist for more?
faq.answer: Vinted allows either side to cancel an order before the item is shipped, and after a cancellation the seller can re-upload it with one tap. A manual cancellation can trigger automatic negative feedback, but the cancellation itself is not blocked. When buyers report the cancel-and-relist pattern, outcomes vary — some report action being taken, others report none.

faq.question: Can I leave negative feedback if a seller cancels my order?
faq.answer: You can't leave a brand-new review, because Vinted only allows feedback on completed orders. But Vinted posts automatic negative feedback on the cancelling member's profile, and as the buyer you can edit or delete that automatic feedback (seller's profile → their star rating → Edit). Editing it to describe what happened is the practical way to warn future buyers.

faq.question: Can I force the seller to honour the sale and send the item?
faq.answer: No. There is no way to compel a seller to ship, and the sale is treated as cancelled once they cancel it. You are refunded automatically. Reporting and accurate feedback are the only levers open to you.

faq.question: Will Vinted ban a seller who keeps cancelling orders?
faq.answer: Sometimes, but not reliably. Some buyers report a repeat canceller's account being actioned after a report; others report nothing happening. A seller can also avoid visible negative feedback by choosing an 'agreed' cancellation reason, which is why a clean-looking profile doesn't always mean an honest seller.

faq.question: Can I get compensation if a Vinted seller cancels my order?
faq.answer: No. A cancelled order is refunded in full, but Vinted does not compensate buyers for the lost item or wasted time. You get your money back and nothing more.

faq.question: The seller cancelled and relisted it higher — should I just pay the new price?
faq.answer: Usually not. Paying the higher price rewards the behaviour, and there is nothing stopping the same seller from cancelling again once the item is back up. Most buyers decide to walk away; if the item is genuinely rare, weigh whether you are comfortable with the risk of another cancellation.
